# Deployments

Read these rules before you archive a deployment, an upgrade, or a hotfix. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

<a id="nr-76"></a>

## NR-76: One folder per stack `[HOLD]`

> Each deployed stack has one folder, `deployments/<chain>/<stack>/`, that holds only event folders, `aborted/`, and a `README.md`.

Old number: 8.1.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Issues: I-10.

`deployments/<chain>/<stack>/`, where `<chain>` is a host chain of
`fhevm-chains.config.json` and `<stack>` the stack's `deploymentId`. Under a stack: event folders, `aborted/` and a
`README.md`, nothing else.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-77"></a>

## NR-77: Event folders are numbered `[GAP]`

> An event folder is named `<seq>-<deploy|upgrade|hotfix>-v<release>-<YYYY-MM-DD>`, with a sequence that starts at `00` and has no gap.

Old number: 8.1.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: `fhevm-npm/base/checks/deployments.ts:346-357` accepts any journal transaction between `first` and `last` as an upgrade's or hotfix's `defining`; it never checks that it is the `ACLOwner.upgrade` transaction. Fix: check it (issue I-67).

Issues: I-10, I-67.

`<seq>-<deploy|upgrade|hotfix>-v<release>-<YYYY-MM-DD>`, the sequence
contiguous from `00`, exactly one `deploy`, first. `v<release>` is the package version the tool ran at, without the
major below 1.0 (`v14.1` is 0.14.1) and with it from 1.0 on (`v1.0.0`); the date is the UTC day of the block holding
the event's defining transaction (an upgrade's or hotfix's `ACLOwner.upgrade`, a deploy's last transaction), as
recorded in the `event.json` of the folder the config's `outDir` names. For now, a deploy without `event.json` ([NR-79](../entries/NR-79.md))
has no recorded block day, so its date is held only to the order of dates ([NR-82](../entries/NR-82.md)).

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-78"></a>

## NR-78: Attempts are outside the sequence `[GAP]`

> An unfinished attempt that sent transactions goes under `aborted/`, outside the event sequence.

Old number: 8.1.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: `first` is only required to be in the journal at its block (:337-340), not to be the journal's lowest block. An attempt whose event.json names a later journal transaction as `first` and `defining`, with the folder named by that later day, passes. Fix: issue I-118.

Issues: I-10, I-118.

An attempt that sent transactions and was not finished goes under
`aborted/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<kind>-v<release>-<n>/`, dated by its first transaction. It never carries a `verify-report.json`
and is never a `previous`.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-79"></a>

## NR-79: Complete and self-consistent `[GAP]`

> Each record holds its config, its tool commit, and the files its kind requires in its out dir, and no scratch or `.git`.

Old number: 8.2.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: `.git` is looked up only at the record root (:202) and the scratch names only directly under the out dir (:253). `<record>/out/.git`, `<record>/out/lib/forge-std/.git`, or scratch one level off (`<record>/cache/` beside an out dir named `out`, `<record>/out/sub/broadcast/`) all pass. deployments/.gitignore keeps the usual scratch names out of a commit, but not `.git`, `build-check` or `rehearsal`. Fix: issue I-119.

Issues: I-10, I-57, I-69, I-119.

`<kind>.config.json` with `deploymentId` = the stack and a relative `outDir`
inside the folder; `tool-commit.txt` whose first line is a full commit (equal to the manifest's `toolCommit` when it has
one); the out dir holds `manifest.json`, `addresses.sol`, `journal.jsonl` and `event.json`, and for an upgrade or hotfix
event `progress.jsonl` and `verify-report.json`; no forge scratch, no `.git`. For now, a deploy may omit `event.json`;
an upgrade, a hotfix and an attempt of any kind may not.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-80"></a>

## NR-80: Identity `[GAP]`

> The manifest of a record states the stack, the chain, the admin, the generation, and the package version that its folders name.

Old number: 8.2.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: The comparison runs only when the config's `admin` is a string (:282). Delete `admin` from hotfix.config.json, or write it as a number: the check passes. Both committed configs carry it. issue I-69 lists this as check behaviour no rule states. Fix: issue I-69.

Issues: I-10, I-57, I-69.

The manifest's `deploymentId` is the stack, its `chainId` the chain folder's, the config's `admin`
the sealed one. In an event folder, the manifest's `version` is the generation, `<major>.<minor>` (`0.14`, `1.0`), and
its `packageVersion` `<major>.<minor>.<p>`, as the folder name says: `v14.1` is `0.14.1`, `v1.0.0` is `1.0.0`. For now,
a deploy's manifest may omit `packageVersion`, and then no manifest field checks the patch in its folder name; an
upgrade or hotfix event's may not.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-81"></a>

## NR-81: Dated by the chain `[HOLD]`

> The date of an event folder is the block day of its defining transaction, never the clock of the operator.

Old number: 8.2.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Issues: I-10, I-67, I-69.

`event.json`'s `defining`, `first` and `last` transactions are in the journal at the
blocks it claims, with `first.block <= defining.block <= last.block`; `defining` is `last` for a deploy event and
`first` for an attempt of any kind. The folder's date is `defining`'s block day. For now, a deploy without `event.json`
([NR-79](../entries/NR-79.md)) names no `defining` transaction, and its folder's date is compared with no block day. The journal's own
timestamps are the operator's clock and date nothing.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-82"></a>

## NR-82: Kinds move versions one way `[HOLD]`

> An upgrade moves one generation up, a hotfix raises the patch, and versions and dates never go back.

Old number: 8.3.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Issues: I-10, I-66.

An upgrade moves exactly one generation up; a hotfix stays in its generation with
a higher patch. Over the sequence, `(generation, patch)` strictly increases and dates never go back. Between consecutive
events that both have an `event.json`, defining blocks strictly increase (for now, a deploy may lack one: [NR-79](../entries/NR-79.md)).

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-83"></a>

## NR-83: Each event links to the one before `[GAP]`

> Every event except a deploy links to the manifest of the event before it, by path and sha256.

Old number: 8.3.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: `fhevm-npm/base/checks/deployments.ts:646-648` finds an attempt's target by exact path, so an attempt that links through a byte-identical copy in its own folder fails before the copy allowance runs. Fix: find the target by the copy's sha256 (issue I-59, decision D15).

Issues: I-10, I-59, I-68.

A deploy has no `previous`. Every other event's manifest has
`previous.path` resolving to the previous event's manifest, `previous.sha256` equal to that file's bytes, and
`previous.deploymentId`, `chainId`, `version`, `packageVersion` equal to it. An attempt links the same way to the event
it started from. The sha256 is the link and the path only says where those bytes are, so the path may instead resolve to
a copy of that manifest kept inside the event's own folder, provided its bytes are identical: what an operator's seal says
when `previousManifest` pointed at a copy. A seal is never rewritten ([NR-84](../entries/NR-84.md)), so such an event could not otherwise be
archived. Through such a copy, and only there, `previous.packageVersion` may be absent when the previous manifest has
none: the folder name that stands for it was out of the tool's sight.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks this rule. It runs in `make check-pre`, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-84"></a>

## NR-84: A record never changes `[HOLD]`

> Nothing under an event or attempt folder that exists at the merge base changes.

Old number: 8.4.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments --base main`

Issues: I-10.

Against a base ref, nothing under an event or attempt folder that exists at the
merge base may be added, modified, deleted, renamed or retyped, committed or not. Locally, an untracked new file is
judged once git tracks it. New event folders, new stacks and READMEs are free.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments --base <ref>` checks this rule. It runs in the workflow `sdk-cleartext-deployments` on every pull request, and it is generation-free.

<a id="nr-85"></a>

## NR-85: The legacy relocation `[HOLD]`

> A flat legacy record may move once into a `00-deploy` event folder, as a pure move.

Old number: 8.4.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check deployments --base main`

Issues: I-10.

A flat record (`<stack>/deploy.config.json`, the layout before events
had folders) may move into `<stack>/00-deploy-v<release>-<YYYY-MM-DD>/` once, as a pure move: every file renamed with
identical bytes to the same relative path under one such folder, nothing added to it; as in [NR-84](../entries/NR-84.md), an untracked new file
is judged once git tracks it. Until then it is checked as a record and reported as a note.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check deployments` checks a legacy record that has not moved, and reports it as a note. It runs in `make check-pre`. `fhevm-npm check deployments --base <ref>` checks a record that moved. It runs in the workflow `sdk-cleartext-deployments` on every pull request. Both are generation-free.
